lines.text: נָשָׁה 700 נָשַׁק
נָשַׁת
Hiph. i. q. Kal no. 1, with בְּ of pers.
to lend to any one on usury, Deut. 15, 2.
Deriv. נְשִׁי, מַשֶּׁה, pr. n. יְשִׁיָּה.
נָשֶׁה m. Gen. 32, 33, i. q. Arab. نَسًا,
prob. nervus ischiadicus, the nerve or
tendon extending through the thigh and
leg to the ankles. R. נָשָׁה I. 1; see
Thesaur. p. 921 sq.
נְשִׁי m. debt, 2 K. 4, 7. R. נָשָׁה II.
נְשִׁיָּה f. forgetfulness, oblivion, Ps. 88,
נָשִׁים plur. f. women, see sing. אִשָּׁה.
נְשִׁיקָה f. (r. נָשַׁק) a kiss, Cant. 1, 2.
Prov. 27, 6.
* נָשַׁךְ, fut. יִשֹּׁךְ Ecc. 10, 11, and יִשַּׁךְ
Prov. 23, 32, to bite, as a serpent Gen.
Mic. 3, 5. Eth. ነሰከ id. Syr. by transp.
ܢܟܰܬ.—Metaph. a) to vex, to oppress,
Hab. 2, 7. b) to lend on usury, Deut.
23, 20; since not only the lending on
usury, but even the taking of interest,
was regarded as sordid and oppressive.
Comp. Aram. נְכַת, ܢܟܰܬ, to bite, whence
נוֹכְתָא usury; Arab. قرض to gnaw,
Conj. III to lend on usury; Gr. δάκνε-
σθαι ὑπὸ τῶν χρεῶν Aristoph. Nub. 1. 12;
Lat. ‘usura vorax’ Lucan. 1. 171.
Piel i. q. Kal, to bite, Num. 21, 6. Jer.
Hiph. הִשִּׁיךְ caus. of Kal lett. b, to take
usury of any one, to exact interest, with
dat. of pers. Deut. 23, 20. 21.—Hence
נֶשֶׁךְ m. in pause נָשֶׁךְ Ex. 22, 24,
usury, interest, Prov. 28, 8. Ps. 15, 5.
Ez. 18, 8. 13. שִׂים נֶשֶׁךְ עַל to impose
usury upon any one, to exact it from
him, Ex. 22, 24; c. לְ Deut. 23, 30. לָקַח
נֶשֶׁךְ מִן to take usury from any one Lev.
נִשְׁכָּה a cell, see לִשְׁכָּה and note.
* נָשַׁל, fut. יִשַּׁל intrans. in no. 2. b;
imper. שַׁל Ex. 3, 5. Josh. 5, 15.
1. Trans. a) to draw out or off, to
put off, e. g. a shoe Ex. 3, 5. Josh. 5, 15.
b) to cast out, to eject a people from a
land Deut. 7, 1. 22.—Kindr. are שָׁלַל,
שָׁלָה, נָצַל. Arab. نشل to draw out,
as meat from a pot; نثل to put off a
breastplate, to draw out arrows from a
quiver.
2. Intrans. a) to slip off or away;
Deut. 19, 5 וְנָשַׁל הַבַּרְזֶל מִן־הָעֵץ and if
the iron slippeth from the helve. b) to
fall or drop off, as the fruit of the olive
Deut. 28, 40, where fut. A. Correspond-
ing is Arab. نسل to fall off, as hair,
wool, feathers.
Piel i. q. Kal no. 1. b, to cast out, to
drive out, a people 2 K. 16, 6.
* נָשַׁם to breathe; Chald. Syr. id.
Arab. نسم to blow gently, as the wind;
V, to breathe. Kindred roots are נָשַׁב,
נָשַׁף, by transp. נָפַּשׁ, comp. Arab. نفس
anhelavit, also parturivit, peperit.—Not
found in the verb; since fut. אֶשֹּׁם Is. 42,
14, as elsewhere fut. יִשֹּׁם, belongs to
the root שָׁמֵם.
Deriv. תִּנְשֶׁמֶת and
נְשָׁמָה f. constr. נִשְׁמַת, c. suff. נִשְׁמָתִי,
plur. נְשָׁמוֹת.
1. breath, spirit, spoken of the breath
of God, i. e. a) the wind, i. q. רוּחַ יְיָ,
Job 37, 10. b) the breath, breathing, of
his anger Is. 30, 33. Job 4, 9. Ps. 18, 16.
c) the spirit of God, imparting life and
wisdom, Job 32, 8. 33, 4; comp. 26, 4.
2. breath, life, of man and beasts;
Gen. 2, 7 and breathed into his nostrils
נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים the breath of life; more fully
נִשְׁמַת רוּחַ חַיִּים Gen. 7, 22. Simpl. נְשָׁמָה
something vain and fleeting Is. 2, 22.—
Hence, anima, the vital spirit, ψυχή, i. q.
נֶפֶשׁ no. 2, plur. Is. 57, 16.
3. the mind, intellect, i. q. נֶפֶשׁ no. 3,
4. Concr. i. q. נֶפֶשׁ no. 4, living thing,
animal; e. g. כָּל־נְשָׁמָה every thing that
hath breath, Deut. 20, 16. Josh. 10, 40.
נִשְׁמָא Chald. f. breath, life, Dan.
* נָשַׁף to breathe, to blow, Ex. 15, 10;
c. בְּ to blow upon, Is. 40, 24.—Kindred
are נָשַׁב, נָשַׁם, also שָׁאַף, by transp. נָפַשׁ.
Arab. نسف to winnow.
Deriv. יַנְשׁוּף and
נֶשֶׁף m. in pause נָֽשֶׁף Job 7, 4; c. suff.
נִשְׁפוֹ Job 3, 9.

line_status.note: The crop is a full running header with three items: Reading A omits the page number 700 and the right-hand catchword נָשַׁק (shin with patach, final qof), which are clearly printed.
Over the sīn of the Arabic word two parallel strokes (fathatān ً) are printed, not a single fatḥa; so نَسًا (B), not نَسَا (A). Hebrew נָשֶׁה and the rest agree in both.
Final word: vowel under shin is a flat pathach bar (no descender), not qamets — compare the clear qamets under nun in נָשַׁךְ. Everything else is identical in both readings and matches the print.

A Syriac vowel point (pthaha, the small inverted-v mark) is clearly printed above the kaph in ܢܟܬ; Reading A omits it, Reading B has it. Everything else in the line is identical between the two readings and matches the print.

The mark after "b" has a descending tail below the baseline, so it is a comma, not a period; the Hebrew (hiriq, shin with dagesh and shin dot, yod, final kaf with sheva) is identical in both readings and matches the print.

Decisive difference is the vowel under the nun of the pausal form: the print shows a qamets (short vertical foot visible under the nun, not the three-dot segol of the headword), giving נָשֶׁךְ as expected for pause; shin dot, segol under shin, and shewa in final kaph are printed in both forms.

The last word is printed שׁ‑ל‑ל (shin, lamed, lamed with qamets + patach), i.e. שָׁלַל; Reading B substituted the entry headword נָשַׁל, which is not what is printed. The following line continues with שָׁלָה, נָצַל, confirming a list of kindred roots.
The pe of נפש is printed with a dagesh (dot visible inside the bowl), so Reading B is correct; everything else is identical in both readings.

The print has a visible space before the semicolon ("verb ;", as in B) AND a dagesh in the shin of אֶשֹּׁם (as in A; the shin carries the shin-dot, holem and an interior dot, matching the Is. 42:14 form from נשם). A drops the space, B drops the dagesh, so neither is exact.

Under the yod the print shows a single dot (hiriq), not a qamets, and the shin carries a dagesh inside it in addition to shin-dot and holem — matching Reading A (יִשֹּׁם, the expected fut. of geminate שָׁמֵם); Reading B's qamets and missing dagesh are not printed.
Under the first mem the print shows two separate dots side by side (tsere), not a solid horizontal stroke (patach); this matches Gesenius's lemma form שָׁמֵם, so Reading A is correct.

The pausal form does carry an accent mark under the nun (Reading B omits it), but it is a vertical stroke (metheg/silluq ֽ, as expected for the verse-final word in Job 7:4), not the wedge-shaped atnach ֑ that Reading A gives.
